newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Yachting - Peter Campbell's Rhumbline Column.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Yachting - Peter Campbell's Rhumbline Column.

text.p: By Peter Campbell*
BRINDABELLA BID FOR LORD HOWE RECORD
One thing about course records in offshore yacht racing is that, no matter how fast your boat is and how well it is sailed, the end result always hinges on the wind, its strength and its direction.

We all know that the Sydney-to-Hobart record has stood unchallenged for 21 years, since the U.S. maxi ketch Kialoa set a time of 2 days 14 hours 36 minutes 56 seconds in a rollicking, mostly downwind ride down the New South Wales south coast, across Bass Strait and down the Tasmanian east coast.
Kialoa broke the existing race record set two years earlier by another remarkable maxi, the ferro cement-hulled 72-footer Helsal, described by yachties as "The Flying Footpath".

Helsal, owned by Sydney medico Dr TONY FISHER, set many race records, including a time of 47 hours 52 minutes 42 seconds in the inaugural race from Gosford-to-Lord Howe Island in 1974 which, unlike her Hobart record, was to stand untouched for 14 years. That record was broken by FISHER himself with his new yacht Helsal II in 1988.
Both yachts were designed by JOE ADAMS, with the original Helsal a fat, double-ended cutter and Helsal II, a lean racing machine. Both revelled in downwind conditions.

This weekend Helsal II's record of 40 hours 23 minutes 31 seconds for the 408-nautical mile course will be on the line when Australia's current fastest maxi, GEORGE SNOW's Brindabella, leads the fleet to sea in the Fujitsu 23rd Gosford-to-Lord Howe Island Yachting Classic.
The Jutson-designed 76-footer had the record in sight in last year's race until she broke her mast halfway to Lord Howe Island, returning some 250 nautical miles under jury rig and motor.

This year Brindabella has a bigger rig and is in winning form. Last weekend she took the line and International Measurement System (IMS) handicap double in the Cruising Yacht Club's Lion Island/Botany Bay race, while a couple of weeks back she broke the Sydney-Bird Island-Sydney race record.
FAMOUS OLD-TIMERS FOR LORD HOWE

There are several bottles of rum on the line in a duel to Lord Howe Island between the crews of two of the most famous timber ocean racing yachts of the late 1960s and 1970s -- Margaret Rintoul II and Love and War.
Margaret Rintoul II was the original Ragamuffin, winning the famous Fastnet Race in England in 1969 when owned by SYD FISCHER.

Now owned by RICHARD PURCELL, she won the Lord Howe Island race last year on IMS corrected time and PURCELL is keen to reverse the result from the 50th Sydney-to-Hobart when Love and War beat her in the 20-year Veteran Division.
Love and War is owned by veteran yachtsman PETER KURTS, chairman of Peter Kurts Properties, the Queensland-based property and investment company.
With her he won two Sydney-to-Hobarts and represented Australia in the Admiral's Cup.
KURTS has put together a strong racing crew, including several who sailed with him in those two Hobart wins, among them PETER SHIPWAY, PHIL EADIE and JOHN HARRIS.
BIG FLEET FOR GASCOIGNE CUP

The Royal Sydney Yacht Squadron has received nearly 100 entries for its prestigious Gascoigne Cup short ocean races off Sydney Heads on Saturday, including many likely competitors in this year's Telstra Sydney-to-Hobart.

Making its racing debut will be the IAIN MURRAY-designed Bashford/Howison-36, Bashfull, owned by DAVID FULLER, the immediate past commodore of the Cruising Yacht Club, and HUGO VAN KRETSCHMAR, the Club's vice-commodore.

FULLER, chief executive of Associated Plastics Industries (API) and VAN KRETSCHMAR, a civil engineer who now runs his own property development company, Bay Developments, have had a long association in sailing, particularly in the Etchell class.

Other entries include two Kenwood Cup team yachts -- SYD FISCHER's Ragamuffin and BOB STEEL's Quest -- along with MARTIN JAMES's Infinity III and TONY PAOLA's Condor of Currabubula, favourite for line honours in the absence of Brindabella.
YOUNG CREW FOR LEXCEN REGATTA
New South Wales will be represented in this year's Westpac Lexcen Regatta in Perth by a young but talented crew from the Royal Prince Alfred Yacht Club (RPAYC).
Skipper JAMES SPITHILL at 17 will be the youngest helmsman in the history of the event.
The Lexcen Regatta, held every year to commemorate the late BEN LEXCEN, that great character of Australian yachting and designer of the America's Cup winning yacht, Australia II.
These days it is a national fleet and match racing championship between crews nominated by each state and is sailed in one-design Foundation-36 sloops. The regatta runs for a week from Sunday.
Sailing with SPITHILL will be other teenagers NATHAN ELLIS, TIM MONTAGUE, NIGEL HORTON and PHIL LINDSAY, all members of the RPAYC and four of them graduates of the club's youth development program.

Last month SPITHILL steered an RPAYC team to second place in the Governor's Cup in California and his Pittwater High School team to second in the national secondary schools team racing championship in Sydney.
ELLIS captained the winning RPAYC team at the Nagy Cup event, sailed in Laser dinghies in San Francisco.
SYDNEY-HOBART NOMINATIONS CLOSING
Next Friday, November 1, is the deadline for yacht owners planning to contest the Telstra Sydney-to-Hobart to lodge their applications for entry with the Cruising Yacht Club of Australia (CYCA).

While actual entries do not close until November 29, the CYCA requires applications to enable its sailing committee to check the eligibility of yachts because the 630-nautical mile race is a Category One safety rules event.

Among the 40 or so early applications received so far are Exile, owned by expatriate Australian Warwick Miller, and Elle Racing, the Whitbread-60 being used by Ardrienne Cahalan as the training yacht for her all-woman crew challenging for next year's Whitbread Round the World race.
Other applications coming in are from New Zealand, Germany, the U.S., Britain and from all Australian states.
*Peter Campbell is the editor of Offshore Yachting magazine.
